value.title: Rust SDK and CLI foundation
value.summary: Foundation-only Rust SDK and CLI with shared explicit configuration/diagnostics, independent service construction and real composed proof.
value.confidence: Product scope is explicit; implementation feasibility and exact public contracts require the guide and applicable proof. No acceptance criterion is proven yet.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Establish a useful, embeddable Rust SDK and a thin standalone CLI for Unisphere before native telemetry normalization is shipped. The first shared operation resolves and validates explicitly supplied source-root configuration and returns structured diagnostics, so this delivery proves real SDK/CLI behavior rather than only compiling empty crates. Components must be independently executable against injected contracts and later composed; services do not wait for a finished CLI. Flowspace3 is the first intended consumer, not the owner of the public model. This product plan is prime-authored; a subsequently assigned PM owns implementation orchestration and peer composition through the reviewed guide.

sections.name: goals
value: A Rust application can consume Unisphere as an ordinary in-process dependency and invoke real foundation behavior without a CLI subprocess, daemon, database or ML service.
Humans and automation can install/run a thin CLI that exposes the same successful and failing foundation operations as the SDK with predictable output and exit behavior.

Provide explicit configuration resolution/validation and actionable typed diagnostics as the first useful shared vertical slice, without prematurely selecting a native-session or telemetry persistence schema.
Make independently testable services and adapters possible from agreed contracts, allowing PM-led parallel construction and later composition without an artificial finished-CLI prerequisite.

Establish reproducible local build, test, architecture and smoke evidence plus developer-facing SDK/CLI documentation; adapt useful Flowspace3 code with preserved provenance rather than copy its server architecture.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Shipping a native session reader, harness discovery sweep, normalization pipeline, historical ingestion or Flowspace3 integration in Plan001; those need separate accepted scope.

Choosing or implementing the final telemetry/session record format, OTLP exporter, archive format, update/rewind semantics, content/counts privacy profiles or durable cursor store in this foundation plan.
A required daemon, HTTP/RPC service, Postgres/SQLite product store, job queue, watcher, model provider, embeddings, pricing engine or git attribution integration.
Registry publication, release automation beyond applicable local/CI proof, cloud deployment, machine-global installs/config changes, hook installation or real private transcript access.

Promoting gitignored scratch reader experiments into shipping code or treating their provisional native-observation contract as the public SDK model; experimentation may proceed independently under the separately authorized scratch scope.
Using Flowspace-specific error codes, configuration fields, truncation policies, PostgreSQL turn schema or summarization scheduling as Unisphere requirements.

value.claim: An external Rust application consumes the SDK from the checkout through ordinary Cargo dependency configuration and invokes the configuration/diagnostic use case in-process, without spawning the CLI or requiring a daemon, database, ML service or caller-created async runtime.

The shared configuration use case accepts a documented minimal configuration for caller-supplied source roots, produces the effective settings and diagnostics deterministically, treats an empty root list as valid, and rejects malformed documents, blank root entries and incompatible value types with field/path-specific errors rather than panicking or substituting guessed values. It does not inspect session content.

Configuration precedence is documented and identical in SDK and CLI: defaults are overridden by explicitly supplied configuration, then explicit caller/CLI overrides; omitted values retain defaults. Library calls do not read ambient HOME, process environment or global config implicitly.

The installable CLI exposes help/version and the shared configuration/diagnostic operation; on equivalent successful and invalid inputs its semantic data/error agrees with direct SDK invocation. A missing or unreadable explicit config file produces a named failure, not success or an empty configuration.

Machine-mode CLI output has a documented versioned success/error envelope and remains parseable without terminal decoration; explicit output selection takes precedence over terminal detection, and piped/captured output defaults to machine mode. Human output is derived from the same result, logs do not corrupt stdout, and successful operations, operational/configuration failures and invalid CLI invocation have documented distinct exit behavior.

Public failures are actionable and typed: callers can distinguish invalid configuration from explicit input I/O failures without parsing prose; CLI failures carry a stable category/code, a useful location when known and remediation guidance, without dumping secrets, full config documents or unrelated session content.

Foundation services are executable in isolation through their public contracts with injected dependencies before a CLI or sibling adapter implementation exists; automated dependency checks reject core/service dependencies on the CLI or concrete outer adapters, and a deliberate forbidden-edge fixture makes the check fail.

Tests and smoke scenarios are deterministic, parallel-safe and isolated from real user configuration/session stores: temporary paths and explicit injected settings are used, foundation operations do not write outside supplied test/workspace paths or start hidden background workers, and ordinary library invocation performs no network calls.

A fresh checkout with the documented Rust toolchain and declared dependencies can build/test the SDK and install/run the CLI locally; SDK consumption and the installed CLI do not require Node/DD/Builder tooling at runtime, repository-private absolute paths, or unpublished sibling binaries.

The repository engineering harness exposes one real product validation lane and a meaningful foundation boot/smoke lane; a passing lane proves the delivered configuration/SDK/CLI behavior and must not claim native telemetry collection or reader support. A deliberately failing product check propagates a failing verdict.

A new consumer can follow documented SDK and CLI examples to reproduce a successful configuration check and an actionable failure; docs state foundation-only capabilities and version/support limits, and any substantial Flowspace3/git-ai code reuse retains applicable licence and provenance notices.

value.title: Usable independent SDK and CLI foundation
value.brief: One integrated outcome checkpoint: external Rust consumption, shared configuration/diagnostics, CLI parity and isolated proof. Internal unit waves are defined by the reviewed guide, not a serial SDK-then-CLI phase order.
value.objective: Deliver real foundation behavior through the SDK and CLI without shipping native readers or settling the telemetry format.
delivers: Public in-process SDK and locally installable CLI
Shared explicit configuration and actionable diagnostics
Independent service contracts and negative dependency checks
Real composed smoke, contributor docs and licence/provenance preservation
value.key_risks: Avoid empty scaffolding, daemon coupling, ambient state and interpreting scratch prototypes or generated teaching guides as approved product contracts.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Inputs: requirements-spine.md (RQ-001–017); original-ask.md; assets/research/otel-common-format.md; pending first-consumer interview assets/requirements/flowspace3-interview.md. Flowspace3 source was reviewed for pure configuration resolution, structured error/envelope behavior, audience-aware output and kind-aware architecture checks. Reuse candidates: crates/core/src/config.rs, catalog.rs, envelope.rs and output.rs; crates/cli/src/render; crates/testkit/src/arch.rs and spawn.rs. Adapt only the parts needed for this product: its daemon/store/ML stack is outside scope. MIT licence in Flowspace3 LICENSE requires retaining notices for substantial copies. OTLP JSONL is a Development-stage official telemetry file scheme, but choosing the eventual telemetry output is a separate workshop, not a dependency for foundation diagnostics.

value.approach: Build behavioral unit/contract tests for configuration resolution and diagnostics, an external-consumer SDK integration check, a real subprocess CLI smoke for success and failure, and a negative dependency-boundary check. Run them through the repository engineering harness once implementation supplies the canonical Rust lane.
value.rationale: The project currently has no product source or runnable product proof. Harness onboarding tests are not SDK proof. Pure tests alone cannot establish CLI/library parity, and an architecture diagram cannot catch a reverse dependency.
value.focus_areas: Explicit configuration precedence; empty/invalid configuration; deterministic diagnostics; SDK/CLI semantic parity; machine/human rendering; caller-controlled side effects; injected service independence; clean checkout consumption; negative dependency drift; sealed temporary HOME/config/fixtures.
value.excluded: Native reader correctness, telemetry schema compatibility, collector round trips, real vendor stores and pricing are not Plan001 acceptance. Scratch experiment tests remain separate and cannot make foundation ACs pass.
value.mock_usage: Prefer injected deterministic fakes and temporary filesystem fixtures at real variation boundaries; use real Rust caller/CLI composition for integration. Do not introduce a trait or mocking framework solely to satisfy a plumbing assertion.

value.location: Public SDK rustdoc and a concise repository CLI/development guide with executable usage examples; source provenance/licence notices for adapted Flowspace3 or other borrowed code.
value.rationale: A new Rust consumer and a terminal user must be able to build, call, diagnose and verify the delivered foundation without inspecting internal source. Clearly label unimplemented reader/format capabilities and keep architecture details in the implementation guide rather than duplicate them here.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: Foundation-only scope was explicitly selected by Jordan. The first real operation is configuration inspection/validation, not a fake reader or a claim that telemetry collection works. Assume an explicitly supplied configuration document and caller overrides are sufficient initially; do not silently import ambient user configuration. The exact configuration shape, SDK/CLI signatures, crate topology, worker units/waves and code-level checks belong to the reviewed implementation guide. The outstanding Flowspace3 interview can refine later reader integration but does not block an independent library/configuration foundation. Product intent ready does not imply guide approval, baseline sealing, dispatched peers or any completed AC.

value.topic: Common telemetry output fields and encoding
value.why: Choose how standard OTel/GenAI fields, source-reconstruction facts and explicit pij identity/role metadata coexist without inventing a competing standard unnecessarily.
value.key_questions: Canonical OTLP LogsData versus standard-aligned typed model/projection; pij peer names/roles/lineage provenance; unknowns, privacy, revisions and versioning.
value.status: Requested by operator; separate from foundation-only delivery and not yet approved.

value.question: Foundation only, or foundation plus the first native-session reader?
value.answer: Jordan selected Foundation only: public Rust SDK, thin CLI, real shared configuration/diagnostic behavior, dependency boundaries, packaging and tests; no native-session reader in this plan.

value.question: Who authors the plan and orchestrates implementation?
value.answer: Operator ruling: primes write the initial product plan; assigned PMs later orchestrate implementations with their peers. Initial plan authorship stays here; no implementation release is granted by this document.

value.question: Must service work wait for the CLI implementation?
value.answer: No. Jordan requires separate agents to build services and components against agreed contracts and compose them later; only true contract dependencies may precede independent work, not completion of the CLI or sibling implementation.

value.question: May native reader work start concurrently with the foundation?
value.answer: Jordan separately authorized Rust service/adapter experiments in gitignored scratch. They are not shipping Plan001 readers, do not expand its ACs, and do not settle the output schema.

value.question: Has the canonical telemetry output format been selected?
value.answer: No. An official Development-stage OTLP JSONL file format was found; a requested output-format workshop compares direct OTLP use with a typed session model plus projection. Foundation command-result formatting is a separate contract.

value.effect: Operator authorized foundation-only product planning and independently constructible services; primes author initial plans and PMs later orchestrate peers.
Standard OTLP JSONL/GenAI field research informs a separate output-format workshop; this plan does not settle the telemetry format.
First-consumer needs remain unconfirmed; no Flowspace-specific indexing policy is imported or treated as blocking for foundation-only scope.
Known Builder defect row37; not Unisphere architecture and not dispatch authority. A real reviewed guide is required before implementation.

value.finding: The SDK/CLI foundation can be useful before native readers or the final telemetry schema exist.
value.action: Deliver one real shared configuration/diagnostic operation and prove both independent SDK consumption and CLI parity.

value.finding: Flowspace3 earns adapter traits only at real variation points and keeps core free of runtime IO, but its application services live in a daemon crate.
value.action: Reuse pure/configuration/error/testing ideas; expose Unisphere application behavior directly through the library, not through a required daemon.

value.finding: Parallelism comes from agreed contracts and independent execution, not separate source files.
value.action: Require service-level proof without CLI/sibling implementations, then a distinct assembled-behavior proof after PM composition.

value.risk: An SDK-shaped crate merely forwards to the CLI/server, making embedded use and independent development impossible.
value.mitigation: External Rust caller proof and service-only tests must succeed without a CLI subprocess/server; forbid reverse dependency edges.

value.risk: Copying Flowspace3 imports its database/ML dependencies, global configuration assumptions or product-specific policies.
value.mitigation: Adapt a documented minimal reuse set, retain licences, review dependency boundaries and exclude server/indexing policies.

value.risk: A foundation implementation becomes only empty crates and help/version output.
value.mitigation: Require the same real configuration-resolution/diagnostic operation through external SDK invocation and installed CLI success/error smoke.

value.risk: Undecided telemetry format or pending consumer preferences stall all component development.
value.mitigation: Keep telemetry readers/format selection out of Plan001; specify foundation interfaces in the guide so independent services/CLI/tests can proceed and compose later.

value.risk: Tests or diagnostics read actual HOME, credentials or native sessions and pass only on one developer machine.
value.mitigation: Explicit injected settings, sealed subprocess environments and temporary fixtures; verify the foundation leaves external state untouched.

value.risk: Builder-generated converter guide is mistaken for Unisphere architecture.
value.mitigation: Known harness defect row 37: the populated teaching guide remains unapproved and must be replaced during the real guide stage, never used for dispatch.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Prime owns initial product intent; PM owns later implementation orchestration, peer packets and assembled delivery. Planning does not appoint a runtime prime or release implementation.

Use the reviewed guide to define contracts before fan-out; release independent components together where their true dependencies allow it. Services must not depend on a completed CLI or same-wave sibling implementation.
Use first-class harness Builder allocation/readiness/dispatch/composition operations and report dogfood problems to pij-varied-alpaca; never replace failed gates with assumptions or bypasses.
The permanent orphan governance branch remains separate; canonical product plan/guide/code/evidence stay on the product plan branch. Direct plan authoring does not mutate canonical flow state.
No generated task, plan AC, contract baseline, review or proof receipt is marked complete before actual applicable evidence exists.
Scratch native readers are separately authorized experiments, gitignored and not imported by shipping crates; promotion requires later accepted product scope and review.
